blocks.text: Condo buildings in Chilliwack Proper West
The Robson — 9450 Robson Street

The building directory records The Robson as built in 2022, with 60 units, amenities elevator, garden and in-suite laundry, and strata bylaws recorded as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. Current listings record the building differently on year: multiple listings state built 2023, with sub-type Apartment/Condo (one records Apartment), 4 storeys, freehold strata ownership, frame-wood construction, underground parking, and listing amenity sets that add clubhouse, exercise centre and caretaker to the directory's list. Listings describe the building as in the revitalized downtown core, a short walk to District 1881.
Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Chilliwack Proper West is the west half of "Chilliwack Proper," the board grouping for the city-proper (downtown-side) part of Chilliwack, as distinct from the Sardis / Vedder / Garrison side south of Highway 1. Nearby areas: Chilliwack Proper East and downtown Chilliwack (District 1881) to the east, Fairfield Island to the north, and Sardis / Vedder Crossing south of Highway 1.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the downtown/hospital side. The one apartment-condo building known by name stands on Robson Street in the revitalized downtown core near District 1881, and the townhouse stock clusters on Wolfe Road across from Townsend Park.
District structure: SD33 has nineteen elementary schools (Kindergarten to Grade 5), four middle schools (Grades 6 to 8), two K-8 schools and five secondary schools (Grades 9–12).

Flood and ALR: flood hazard zoning exists in the bylaw structure (RS-FHA reserve zone, Section 12.02 of Bylaw No. 5000) and the City applies flood protection requirements and a Floodplain Regulation Bylaw. Properties in the Agricultural Land Reserve are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR regulations, and the City directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).
This market runs on a different board's numbers — or none. Chilliwack trades on CADREB, SnapStats does not cover the city, and CADREB publishes board-wide figures only.

The Robson's build year disagrees between the directory and its own listings. Directory: 2022. Listings: 2023, consistently. The difference matters for warranty stage and depreciation-report timing, and it settles only on the registered strata plan — a buyer's agent should not repeat either year as settled until then.

The downtown condo sits inside a form-and-character permit area. OCP Bylaw 5500's Schedule D-6 makes the whole downtown a Form & Character Development Permit Area under Local Government Act s. 488(1)(d), with the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan and Downtown Design Guidelines behind it — exterior alterations and redevelopment around The Robson run through that lens, not just the zoning bylaw.

The hospital is the area's true anchor, and it is a Fraser Health community hospital — primary, core secondary and some specialty services at 45600 Menholm Road, on the Hodgins Avenue side of the Proper West ground, minutes from both the Robson Street and Wolfe Road strata stock.

items.t: Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. Board identity: a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market, not a Fraser Valley or Greater Vancouver board market; CADREB's territory description covers a regional area from Yarrow to Lytton including Chilliwack, and CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables.
The page describes detached homes, ranchers, infill duplexes and small-lot homes, strata townhomes and low-rise condos near the hospital precinct.

Planning geography: the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan is Schedule B-2 of the Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, and the City's 2050 OCP review incorporated the plan's land uses into city-wide designations.

Anchor institution: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, at the Hodgins Avenue / Menholm Road precinct on this side of the city — Fraser Health describes it as a community hospital providing primary, core secondary and some specialty services.
No other board's figures are substituted.
There are no Chilliwack market statistics to quote — from anyone. Price land and houses from the property's own CADREB comparables.

Proper West's plan is a schedule, not the city-wide text alone: the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan sits as Schedule B-2 of OCP Bylaw No. 5500, and the 2050 OCP review folded its land uses into city-wide designations while its neighbourhood policies remain in the plan — a lot buyer reading only the OCP's general residential policies misses the Proper-specific layer.
Tax penalty dates are Chilliwack-specific: 5% after July 2, 2026 and a second 5% after August 4, 2026 — not the September second-penalty date used by some neighbouring cities.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: streets and boundaries

items.t: Chilliwack Proper West has no official boundary: it is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) sub-area name for the western part of Chilliwack Proper, and the City of Chilliwack publishes no boundary for it.

The working orientation is the grid west of the downtown core, around Young Road, Corbould Street and the airport side of Chilliwack Proper, taken from the addresses of the schools and facilities on that side rather than from any City map.

The closest official planning area is larger than the sub-area: the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan covers the established residential area of Chilliwack Proper as a whole, and it is Schedule B2 of Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500.
Its neighbours are Chilliwack Proper East and downtown Chilliwack (District 1881) to the east, Fairfield Island to the north, and Sardis and Vedder Crossing south of Highway 1.
Townsend Park, a 15-hectare City park west of downtown, is the area's western green anchor.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is an older urban grid, not a single subdivision: the neighbourhoods plan designations that cover it are Residential 1 (one and two family housing) and Residential 2 (attached housing and narrow lot infill), quoted in a City public hearing notice dated May 4, 2021 for a rezoning inside the plan area.

Infill is the live building story on this side: the Schedule B2 plan's stated purpose is to guide future decision making on residential infill development, and it was first added to the 2040 Official Community Plan (OCP) as Schedule D through Bylaw 2018, No. 4533.
No official source publishes a build-era or strata-versus-freehold split for this sub-area, so any age profile for a specific street is a property-by-property check, not a neighbourhood figure.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Flood rules come first on this side of the city: under the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519, the underside of the lowest habitable floor must be built to the Flood Construction Level (FCL) plus 0.6 metres of freeboard, and no basement is allowed (a crawlspace to 1.5 metres deep is the maximum, subject to drainage rules).

A suite here is capped and singular: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 allows only 1 accessory dwelling unit per lot, a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 square metres and 40% of the building's habitable floor space, and a garden suite is capped at 100 square metres.

A suite must be built with a building permit, meet the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new secondary suites are not permitted below the flood construction level — the rule that bites hardest in this floodplain-side grid.
City-wide rules that also apply here include the small-scale multi-unit housing position in Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395 and the zoning bylaw itself.
Short-term rentals are a regulated operation under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141, adopted November 24, 2021, which repealed the former Bed and Breakfast Bylaw 2003, No. 2968.

Creek-side lots can trigger a second permit layer: Development Permit Area 3 (Riparian Areas) requires a Riparian Areas Protection Regulation assessment report from a qualified professional before subdivision, construction or land alteration in a designated riparian area.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The area's recreation centre is the Chilliwack Landing Leisure Centre at Unit #1, 9145 Corbould Street, with pools, a fitness centre, an outdoor water playground, a skateboard park and a pump track, with The Landing park beside it.
Hope River Corbould Park at 9899 Corbould Street and Evergreen Hall at 9291 Corbould Street put a river-side park and a community hall on the same Corbould Street corridor as the leisure centre.
Chilliwack General Hospital, the city's community hospital at 45600 Menholm Road, sits on this west side of Chilliwack Proper, in the Hodgins Avenue and Menholm Road precinct.
The nearest library branch is outside the sub-area: Chilliwack Library at 45860 First Avenue, in the downtown core to the east.
A legal suite or coach house gets its own civic address through the City's alias address process, which requires an application form and a site plan showing where the suite or coach house sits.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: development and new projects

items.t: Townsend Park amenity building, Townsend Park, Chilliwack Proper West — City of Chilliwack project: a 4,600 square foot storage building was converted into an amenity space with accessible washrooms, a potable water station, sport training equipment storage and multi-use changeroom and meeting space, using $375,800 of federal Build Communities Strong Fund money. Status: completed in 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

Chilliwack Fire Department training facility, Wolfe Road — City of Chilliwack project: a four-storey situational awareness training facility constructed using $1.22 million of the same federal funding. Status: completed in 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: costs and taxes

items.t: City utility and solid waste charges on this side are billed quarterly, under the Waterworks Regulation Bylaw 2004, No. 3702 and the Solid Waste Management Bylaw 2019, No. 4660.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: getting around

items.t: There is no rapid transit in Chilliwack: the closest SkyTrain connection is by bus, on BC Transit Route 66 Fraser Valley Express to Lougheed Town Centre Station.
Route 52 Evans runs from Downtown Chilliwack to Cottonwood Mall via Evans Road, with a timing point at Hodgins Avenue at Ashwell Road, serving the south-western streets of this area.
Route 57 Broadway runs from Downtown Chilliwack to Cottonwood Mall via Young Road, with timing points near the airport and at Young Road.
BC Transit added Sunday-evening service on Routes 52, 53, 54, 57 and 58 and expanded Route 66 on all days of the week in the January 4, 2026 service change.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Proper West: risks and due diligence

items.t: Alluvial fan areas are a separate check on the creek-side streets: a site-specific assessment by a qualified professional is required to set building setback and elevation, and an engineered concrete foundation must extend a minimum of 1.0 metre above grade at any point on the building perimeter.
